one_line: Early Deccan monarch and patron of the Maharashtri Prakrit love-poem tradition later known as the Gaha Sattasai.

appearance.face: oval face with warm medium-brown Deccan complexion, sharp straight nose, well-defined jaw, neatly trimmed short beard and moustache, large thoughtful anime-style eyes with dark irises, default expression calm and observant with a gentle half-smile
appearance.hair: thick black hair, shoulder-length and slightly wavy, drawn back into a low knot at the back of the head; front kept tidy with a narrow gold band circling the forehead like a simple diadem, no crown spikes
appearance.costume: He wears a finely draped ivory-white cotton dhoti wrapped to the ankles with a broad maroon border, pleats falling straight in front; above, a fitted long-sleeved pale gold angarakha-style tunic that overlaps to the right and ties with small knotted cords, its edges trimmed in maroon; over his left shoulder and around the torso runs a soft, lightweight saffron-yellow cotton uttariya (shawl) with a subtle thin red stripe pattern near the ends; his feet are in simple brown leather sandals; jewellery is modest but royal: a single short gold necklace of round beads, two plain gold bangles on each wrist, and small gold stud earrings; overall look is neat, symmetrical, and historically grounded in early Deccan royal dress, with all garments fully covering the torso and legs.
appearance.signature: A rolled palm-leaf manuscript bundle bound with a dark red cord, held in his left hand, and a slender stylus tucked behind his right ear, symbolizing his role as compiler and patron of poets rather than sole author.

ref_desc: King Hala is a lean, medium-brown Deccan ruler with shoulder-length black hair in a low knot, gold forehead band, ivory dhoti with maroon border, pale gold tunic, saffron shawl, simple gold jewellery, brown sandals, and a palm-leaf manuscript bundle with stylus in saffron-gold-maroon tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character sheet of King Hala: a lean early-30s Deccan monarch with an oval medium-brown face, large thoughtful dark eyes, straight nose, and a neat short beard and moustache. His thick black hair falls to the shoulders and is tied into a low knot at the back, circled by a narrow gold band on the forehead. He is fully clothed in era-accurate early Deccan royal dress: an ivory-white cotton dhoti with a broad maroon border, wrapped securely to the ankles with clean front pleats; a long-sleeved pale gold angarakha-style tunic overlapping to the right and tied with simple cords, covering the torso modestly; and a soft saffron-yellow cotton uttariya (shawl) draped from the left shoulder across the chest and around the back, showing thin red stripe detailing near its ends. On his feet are simple brown leather sandals. He wears restrained royal jewellery: a short gold beaded necklace, two plain gold bangles on each wrist, and small gold stud earrings. In his left hand he carries a rolled palm-leaf manuscript bundle tied with a dark red cord, while a slender stylus is tucked behind his right ear, emphasizing his patron-editor persona. Use an ivory, maroon, pale gold, saffron yellow, and brown color palette, and show him from multiple angles to make the face, hair knot, clothing drape, jewellery, sandals, and manuscript prop clearly readable.
